en: Mount Apo, not Mount Mayon, is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Palawan is geographically classified under the Luzon island group, not the Visayas region where many people mistakenly place it.
Taal Volcano is not a single mountain, but a complex volcano featuring a large main crater lake.
The Cagayan River, rather than the shorter Pasig River, holds the title of the longest river in the Philippines.
Laguna de Bay is the largest freshwater lake in the Philippines, not a saltwater sea connected to the ocean.
The Philippine Sea is situated on the eastern side of the archipelago, facing the Pacific Ocean, not the western side.
Mount Pulag is the highest mountain in Luzon, not Mount Apo, which is located further south on the island of Mindanao.
The Philippines experiences a tropical climate with distinct wet and dry seasons, rather than a dry desert climate.
Mount Pinatubo is currently classified as a dormant volcano, not an actively erupting one like people sometimes assume.
The Tubbataha Reefs are geographically located in the middle of the Sulu Sea, not attached to the mainland coast of Palawan.
The Philippine eagle is endemic to the forests of Mindanao, not the northern island of Luzon where it does not live.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are not made of chocolate, but are named for their brown grass during the dry season.
